### Description of the company
Železiarne Podbrezová a.s. sú integrovaným výrobcom ocele a oceľových bezšvíkových rúr so sídlom na strednom Slovensku v obci Podbrezová. Pod značkou ŽP Group sú združené výrobné závody v Slovenskej republike a Španielsku. Predaj spoločnosti je realizovaný v 50 krajinách sveta a to cez vlastnú predajnú a marketingovú sieť.  
História firmy sa začala písať v roku 1840 a je výnimočná najmä tým, že v každej dejinnej etape spoločnosť dokázala čeliť mnohým prekážkam a udržať si špičkové postavenie medzi hutníckymi fabrikami. Železiarne Podbrezová sa od svojho vzniku riadia filozofiou, že úspešnosť a prosperita firmy závisí predovšetkým od ľudí.  
Organizovanému odbornému rastu mladej generácie sa dlhodobo venuje veľká pozornosť. Dnes si spoločnosť pripravuje svojich zamestnancov vo vlastnej Súkromnej spojenej škole ŽP - SSOŠH ŽP a SG ŽP. Výrazná pozornosť je venovaná aj spoločenskému, kultúrnemu a športovému vyžitiu zamestnancov.  
Výrobky sú certifikované podľa TÜV, Lloyd’s Register of Shipping, Germanischer Llloyd, Bureau Veritas, API, Det Norske Veritas. Systém riadenia kvality, manažment odpadov a bezpečnosť práce sú certifikované podľa štandardov ISO a IATF. Kvalitnú výrobu dokumentuje aj mnoho dodávateľských oprávnení napríklad od SAUDI. ARAMCO, Kuwait National Petroleum Company, TOTAL France, SAIPEM Taliansko, Abu Dhabi Company for Onshore Oil Operations a iných.

Železiarne Podbrezová a. s. is the producer of steel and seamless steel tubes based in Podbrezová, Central Slovakia. The company is one of the leading manufacturers of steel tubes in Europe. The history of the company began in 1840 and every period was able to face many obstacles and still maintain an excellent position in the metallurgical industry. Since its inception, Železiarne Podbrezová has had a governing philosophy that the success and prosperity of the company depend primarily on its people. On a long-term basis, careful attention is devoted to organizing the professional development of the young generation. The company is preparing its employees in their own private schools. ## Our history
Železiarne Podbrezová a.s. has a rich history dating back to 1840. Throughout its existence, it has undergone many changes, yet it has always managed to maintain a leading position among metallurgical companies. Today, it is a leader in the production of seamless steel tubes, known worldwide.
**An overview of key milestones that brought progress and laid the foundations for the successful development of Železiarne Podbrezová a.s.:**
### Modern history of the company
**•** 2013 – **[reconstruction of the dedusting systems of the electric arc furnace and ladle furnace](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d6O2-fVr5sw)** , and **[reconstruction of the continuous steel casting facility](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VJMyKuvMWcw)**  
**•** 2010 Commissioning of the line for the production of **[electrolytically galvanized steel tubes](https://www.oceloverury.sk/galvanicky-pozinkovane/)**  
**•** 08/2008 A new subsidiary, **[ŽP Výskumno-vývojové centrum, s.r.o.](https://www.zpvvc.sk/)** , was established in Podbrezová.  
**•** 2008 A major investment, **[ŽP EKO QELET](https://www.ekoqelet.sk/)** – a steel scrap processing plant in Hliník nad Hronom, was completed.  
**•** 07/2008 ŽP Group expanded to include the Spanish company **[Transformaciones Metalúrgicas S.A. (Transmesa)](https://transmesa.com/en)** and its subsidiary TAP Tubos de Acero de Precisión S.L.  
**•** 10/2006 The company obtained the quality management system certification for the automotive industry in accordance with **[ISO/TS 16949](https://www.oceloverury.sk/kontrola-kvality/#IATF-16949)**.  
**•** 09/2006 Opening of **[the Private Secondary Grammar School of ŽP a.s.](https://www.sgzp.sk/)**  
**•** 04/2006 Award for trade fair presentation AURA 2005  
**•** 03/2004 Through ŽĎAS, the company made a capital investment in ŠKODA TS, a.s.   
**•** 03/2003 Transformation of the Metallurgical Vocational School in Podbrezová into **[the Private Secondary Technical School of Metallurgy of ŽP a.s.](https://www.ssszp.sk/)**  
**•** 08/2002 Capital investment of the company in **[ŽĎAS a.s.](https://www.zdas.com/)**  
**•** 06/2000 The company obtained environmental management system certification in accordance with **[EN ISO 14001](https://www.oceloverury.sk/environmentalny-manazment/)**  
**•** 04/2000 The company obtained supplier certification for the automotive industry in accordance with VDA 6.1.  
**•** 1999 Establishment of the joint-stock company ŽP ŠPORT Podbrezová  
**•** 1998 Opening of the **[ŽP SKI Tále](https://www.tale.sk/)** winter sports resort  
**•** 1995 Obtaining certification for **[the quality management system](https://www.oceloverury.sk/kontrola-kvality/)** in accordance with ISO 9002  
**•** 1993 A modern high-performance electric arc furnace was commissioned.  
**•** 1992 The state-owned enterprise was transformed into a joint-stock company.  
**•** 1991 Establishment of the Metallurgical Secondary Production facility for tube processing.  
**1980s – construction of social program facilities, including housing, recreational facilities, and sports complexes.**  
**•** 1984 Introduction of an automated management system  
**•** 1982 Start of the production of cast billets on a four-strand continuous steel casting machine.  
**•** 1980 Opening of the Tube Drawing Mill 2.  
**•** 1979 Start of the production of hot-rolled tubes in the rolling mill with a push bench.  
**•** 1972 Start of the production of precision cold-drawn tubes  
**•** 1971 Drawing of the first tube in the new drawing mill  
**•** 1970 Commissioning of a new line for the production of welded elbows  
**•** 1968 Ceremonial groundbreaking of the construction of a new plant  
**•** 1960 Construction of electric arc furnaces and commissioning of the first continuous steel casting facility in Czechoslovakia  
**•** 1951 Start of the reconstruction of the steelworks and construction of a Siemens–Martin furnace
### History of the steelworks after 1900
**•** 1945 Military operations damaged almost all operational buildings and production facilities.  
**•** 01/1941 Sale to Reichswerke AG für Waffen- und Maschinenbau Hermann Göring, Berlin; the main production program consisted of heavy plates, structural and reinforcing steel, and seamless tubes.   
**•** 06/1930 The first issue of the newspaper **[Podbrezovan](https://www.podbrezovan.sk/)** was published.  
**•** 1930 Construction of a Mannesmann tube rolling mill  
**•** 1926 Start of construction of the section rolling mill  
**•** 1921–1924 Severe economic crisis  
**•** 1919 Renaming of the settlement of Brezová to Podbrezová  
**•** 09/1919 Resumption of production at the fine and medium rolling mills and of sheet production  
**•** 10/1918 Shutdown of production in Brezová  
**•** 1906 Construction of the sheet rolling mill – Lauth trio  
**•** 1904 Start of production of welded tubes using water gas
### Brezová ironworks up to 1900
**•** By the end of the 19th century, the Podbrezová ironworks ranked among the largest and most prosperous ironworks in the Kingdom of Hungary.   
**•** 1892 Construction of the Roman Catholic church in Podbrezová  
**•** 1886 Completion of the reconstruction of the plant under the leadership of Professor Kerpely  
**•** 1884 Railway connection with Banská Bystrica  
**•** 1883 At the initiative of A. Kerpely, Director of the State Ironworks in Budapest, tube production was introduced as the first of its kind in Austria-Hungary.  
**•** 1879 A major milestone of Slovak ironmaking – the first Siemens–Martin furnace  
**•** 1872 First telegraph and telephone connection  
**•** 1862 Medal in London  
**•** 1858 Award for rail quality at the Industrial Exhibition in Paris  
**•** 1855 Production of the first 2,374 tonnes of rails. Sheets, enameled cookware, and cast iron components were exported to Transylvania, Austria, Silesia, and Egypt.   
**•** 09/1851 Start of operation of puddling furnaces
### Establishment of the Brezová ironworks
**•** 1840 Start of the first construction works  
**•** 1839 A commission consisting of G. Schweizer, M. Glanzer, and A. Lobkowitz determined the exact location for the placement of the rolling mill.  
**•** 1838 G. Schweizer, chamber count in Banská Štiavnica, proposed the construction of a rail rolling mill below the Brezová hill.  
**•** 1836 Decision of the Austro-Hungarian Parliament to construct 12 railway lines under Act No. XXV 
### Traditions of ironmaking in the Horehronie region
• **18th century** – in the Horehronie region, the so-called Hrončiansky complex was formed, the most important center of iron production in the entire Kingdom of Hungary.   
• **16th–17th centuries** – an unprecedented expansion of ironmaking, primarily focused on production for the arms industry.  
• **14th century** – the first shaft furnaces (so-called Slovak furnaces) and water-powered hammers were built in the valleys of the Slovak Ore Mountains.

#  Students Praise Their Summer Jobs at Železiarne Podbrezová, Appreciating Both the Team and the Pay 
Summer jobs at Železiarne Podbrezová continue to be very popular among students this year. During the holidays, dozens of young people from secondary schools and universities are helping out in various production operations, gaining not only financial rewards but also valuable work experience.
At the end of the first month of the summer holidays, we spoke to several temporary student workers and asked them to share their impressions. They agree that the main attractions are good earnings, a friendly team, high-quality training, and the opportunity to experience a real working environment.
**They Particularly Appreciate the Team**
Maroš Škoda from the Secondary Industrial School of Transport in Zvolen is working at the steelworks for the first time. “It’s great here. My colleagues are always willing to help me, so I’m satisfied and I haven’t had any problems so far,” he says. He plans to continue working until the end of August and would recommend the summer job to other students as well.
Lea Mišunová from Ján Chalupka Grammar School in Brezno has a similarly positive view of her experience. She works at the defect inspection equipment in the new plant. “I received excellent training and I have great colleagues, so I would definitely choose this summer job again,” she said.
**An Experience Worth Having**
Lukáš Košík from the Jozef Murgaš Secondary Industrial School in Banská Bystrica already worked at the steelworks last year and also returned to work during weekends. In the tube drawing mill, he works as a tube drawer and bundler. In addition to the good team, he also appreciates the financial reward.
Patrik Chriašteľ from the Slovak University of Agriculture in Nitra has been working at the company as a temporary student worker for more than two years. He has worked in several positions and particularly appreciates the possibility of arranging the number and timing of his shifts. “I would recommend this summer job to every young person because it is a good way to earn some extra money and the work is not that demanding,” he says.
**Also an Opportunity to Gain Experience in Their Field**
For some students, a summer job is also an opportunity to learn more about the field they would like to pursue in the future. Adam Švantner from the [**Private Joint School of Železiarne Podbrezová**](https://www.ssszp.sk/) studies electrical engineering and had already gained experience at the steelworks during his school practical training. During the summer, he works on a tube end-pointing machine.
“I’m satisfied, and we also have a great team. Night shifts are more demanding, but they can be managed,” he says. At the same time, he points out that it is important to follow safety rules when working in a production environment.
The experiences of this year’s temporary student workers show that a summer job at Železiarne Podbrezová is not only about earning money. It also gives students new experience, work habits, and an opportunity to learn how a manufacturing company operates.
According to the students themselves, there is certainly no reason to be afraid of giving it a try.

## Podbrezovan 
Podbrezovan has been writing its story since June 1930, when it became the very **first workers’ periodical** in Slovakia. Despite strong persecution and administrative obstacles, the publisher at the time managed to release seven issues. Publication was subsequently suspended for political reasons and resumed several years later.

### Bilingual Beginnings
In 1942–1943, the newspaper was published bilingually in Slovak and German. Since 1945, Podbrezovan has been published continuously—initially as a monthly, later as a biweekly. Throughout its history, the newspaper has reflected developments within the company and society, always with a strong focus on timeliness, employee life, and corporate values. 
### The Newspaper Today
Today, Podbrezovan plays a key role in both internal and external communication. It is not only a traditional bridge between the employer and employees, but also a modern platform for presenting the position of Železiarne Podbrezová a.s. to the wider public.

#  Our People – Our Value 
At Železiarne Podbrezová, we recognise that our employees are the key to long-term prosperity. That is why we systematically build a strong and stable team of professionals, rooted in tradition, professionalism, and responsibility. Human resources are a strategic priority for us, and we approach them comprehensively – from recruitment and education to health, benefits, and working conditions. 
## Social Responsibility and Employee Benefits
Our employee programmes include:
  * contributions for recreation and meals, 
  * contributions to healthcare,
  * contributions to supplementary pension savings,
  * rehabilitation stays, insurance, and contributions for life anniversaries, 
  * social assistance, scholarships, and support for education.


## Supporting Education and Professional Growth
At Železiarne Podbrezová, we believe that company growth starts with people. Every year, we train more than 10,000 individuals across dozens of professional roles – from crane operators and load binders to foremen and technologists. Education is an integral part of our strategic management. We focus on quality, safety, environmental protection, and new technologies. We use both internal and external trainers, cooperate with universities, and support employees in external studies. 
### **Our Strength Lies in Expertise**
Employees are offered opportunities for professional development, part-time study alongside employment, and long-term job stability within one of the largest steelmaking companies in Slovakia. We value long-serving employees and actively support generational renewal. 
We support:
  1. **professional and career** development,
  2. **personal development programmes,**
  3. **study allowances and advisory services,  
**
  4. cooperation with **technical schools and universities.**


As a result, we build a team that keeps pace with the most advanced trends in steelmaking and industry.
## Housing and Support for Life Stability
We also support housing for our employees. Within the group, we offer 120 rental apartments, forming part of a stable and community-oriented living environment in the region.
## Collective Agreement as a Partnership-Based Approach
We view cooperation with the trade union organisation at Železiarne Podbrezová as a cornerstone of our corporate culture. Constructive and factual social dialogue enables us to find a balance between employee needs and company objectives. Each year, together with the**Basic Organisation of OZ KOVO ŽP** – the local branch of OZ KOVO, the Slovak Trade Union of Metalworkers, we negotiate a**collective agreement** governing working conditions, wages, and social benefits. These negotiations are conducted with a strong emphasis on fairness, transparency, and long-term stability. 
**We Guarantee Our Employees:**
  1. fair **wages and wage supplements** (e.g. for night work, weekends, on-call duty),
  2. **meal benefits** and contributions for recreation,
  3. **social assistance** in difficult life situations,
  4. participation in creating a healthy and safe working environment.


**The collective agreement** reflects annual increases in the minimum wage and includes improvements in allowances and employee benefits. This shared agreement strengthens trust between employees and management and contributes to the stability and performance of the entire company.

#  Quality and Integrated Management Systems 
At Železiarne Podbrezová, quality is not only about product parameters – it is our commitment to customers and partners. Every process is guided by the same objectives: **reliability, safety, responsibility, and sustainability**. 
On this page, you will find all key information about our quality standards, certifications, and environmental commitments.
###### Integrated management systems
### **Management Systems**
We have implemented and certified quality, environmental, and occupational health and safety management systems in accordance with **[ISO 9001](https://www.steeltube.sk/quality-control/), [IATF 16949](https://www.steeltube.sk/quality-control/#IATF-16949), [ISO 14001](https://www.steeltube.sk/environmental-management/), [ISO 45001](https://www.steeltube.sk/safety-policy/), [API Spec Q1](https://www.steeltube.sk/steel-tubes-for-petroleum-and-gas-industry/)**, and [**DIEX**](https://www.steeltube.sk/steel-tubes-for-boiler-and-pressure-equipment/#DIEX%E2%80%9312X1MF) standards, ensuring:
  * continuous improvement of production processes
  * a high technical level of products
  * a strong focus on customer satisfaction


📄[[Quality Policy – PDF]](https://www.zelpo.eu/content/uploads/2026/07/Grafika-Politiky-ZP-KVALITA-EN.pdf), 📄 [[Environmental Policy – PDF]](https://www.zelpo.eu/content/uploads/2026/06/Grafika-Politiky-ZP-ENVIRO-EN.pdf), 📄 [[Safety Policy – PDF]](https://www.zelpo.eu/content/uploads/2026/06/Grafika-Politiky-ZP-BOZP-EN.pdf), 📄 [[Certificates – PDF]](https://www.steeltube.sk/quality-management-system/)
###### Product quality and certifications
### **Product Certifications**
Our seamless steel tubes are certified in accordance with European and international standards, including:
  * EN 10210, EN 10216, PED 2014/68/EU
  * TÜV, DNV, Lloyd’s Register, AD 2000 and others


[[View all certificates – PDF]](https://www.steeltube.sk/product-certificatesp1/)
###### **Compliance with European and global legislation**
###  **REACH****& Environmental Compliance**
Our products fully comply with European and international legislation related to chemical safety and environmental protection.
We issue a **Declaration of Conformity** confirming compliance with the following regulations:
[**REACH – Regulation (EC) No. 1907/2006**](https://www.steeltube.sk/reach/)  
We comply with REACH requirements, including the control of SVHC substances.
**RoHS 3 – Directive 2011/65/EU**  
We confirm compliance with restrictions on hazardous substances.
**RoHS 3 – Directive 2011/65/EU**  
We confirm compliance with restrictions on hazardous substances.
**Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 – POPs**  
Our products do not contain persistent organic pollutants.
**Regulation (EU) 2024/573 – Fluorinated Greenhouse Gases**  
We ensure compliance with climate-related regulations.
**Regulation (EU) 2024/590 – Ozone-depleting Substances**  
Our production processes comply with ozone protection legislation.
**Dodd-Frank Act Section 1502 – Conflict Minerals**  
We comply with transparency requirements regarding conflict minerals. 
📄[If you require a declaration, please contact your company representative]
###### Environmental profile of products
### **Carbon Footprint and Environmental Declarations**
We are transparent also in the area of the climate impacts of our products. For our seamless steel tubes, we have prepared a Product Carbon Footprint in accordance with ISO 14067 and the GHG Protocol, providing a clear picture of their environmental impact throughout the entire life cycle. 
We also hold a verified Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) in accordance with ISO 14025, which includes a comprehensive life-cycle assessment (LCA) and represents a key document for sustainable construction and industrial projects.
